service.description: The darpan.audit.report/v1 document for one audit on one morning: report, health, summary, and the four categories with every statement of the audit, its checks and its findings (oldest first, at most 50 per statement). State is as of the end of reportDate, so a past morning reads from the findings' history.

parameter.name: auditId
parameter.description: The audit to report, e.g. GORJANA_MONTH_CLOSE; another tenant's audit reads as not found.

parameter.name: reportDate
parameter.description: The morning to describe, as a tenant calendar day.

parameter.name: period
parameter.description: DAR-BE-091. Which period's run to describe, e.g. 2026-10. Blank: the morning's own period.

parameter.name: generatedStamp
parameter.description: report.generatedAt; pinned by tests, now otherwise.

return.message: Audit ${auditId} was not found for tenant ${companyUserGroupId}

service.description: The audit-run report in its GraphQL shape: assemble#AuditReport with each keyed object turned into a list (contract, "GraphQL mapping"). The audit is named by its code; another tenant's audit reads as not found.

parameter.name: date
parameter.description: The morning, YYYY-MM-DD; blank is today in the tenant's zone.

parameter.name: publicError
parameter.description: Why there is no report, in words a caller may see.

service.description: One finding's document in its GraphQL shape: assemble#AuditFinding with records as a list. A finding of another tenant reads as not found.

parameter.name: publicError
parameter.description: Why there is no finding, in words a caller may see.

service.description: DAR-BE-098, findings(query:). One page of the tenant's findings in their GraphQL shape: each node is the report's finding summary plus its audit, statement, category, period and last sighting, records as a list. The engine parses query: and hands over the terms; the tenant is the request's, never an argument.

parameter.name: searchTerms
parameter.description: The parsed query: terms, [key, comparator, values] each: audit, statement, category, state, period (eq, in) and firstFound (eq, gt, gte, lt, lte).

parameter.name: sortKey
parameter.description: FIRST_FOUND (default) or STATEMENT (catalog order, each oldest first).

parameter.name: after
parameter.description: A cursor from this list, under the same sortKey and reverse.

parameter.name: publicError
parameter.description: Why there is no page, in words a caller may see.

set.from: darpan.audit.AuditReportAssembler.findingsPage(ec, companyUserGroupId, searchTerms, sortKey, reverse, first, after)

service.description: DAR-BE-091. The window an audit's checks read on one morning: from the first day of the audit's period to the report day, inclusive ("on the 14th it reconciles 1-14, on the 15th 1-15"). The scheduled run (DAR-BE-092) asks this before extracting, so every open finding of the period is examined again.

parameter.name: runs
parameter.description: The run the morning owes: [[period, windowFromDate, windowThruDate]].

return.message: Audit ${auditId} was not found for tenant ${companyUserGroupId}

service.description: The darpan.audit.finding/v1 document for one finding: status, records, evidence, diagnosis, how to fix and verify it, and its history. A finding of another tenant reads as not found.
